cfg.groqGuide: No Groq API key yet? Tap here for the setup guide
cfg.groqStep1: Open console.groq.com/keys (goes straight to the API Keys page)
cfg.groqStep2: Sign up or log in with Google, GitHub, or Email (email sign-up needs verification)
cfg.groqStep4: Type any name (e.g. "my notes") and submit
cfg.groqStep5: You will see a key starting with gsk_ — shown only once. Copy it now; it is gone after you leave
cfg.groqStep6: Come back here and paste it into the input above
cfg.groqNote: The free tier needs no credit card and is plenty for daily notes. Keys stay in this device's browser and are never uploaded anywhere.
cfg.ollamaSttDesc: Used when the transcription service is "Local Ollama". Audio only goes to the address below. Default http://127.0.0.1:11434. If unreachable, check: 1) ollama serve is running; 2) cross-origin is allowed (e.g. OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*); 3) the firewall allows port 11434.
cfg.sttModelDesc: Note: plain text models cannot hear audio. Use a speech-capable model (whisper family, qwen2.5-omni, qwen3-omni, gemma3n, etc.). Use the button below to list installed models first.
cfg.fwDesc: Used when the transcription service is "Faster-Whisper". Tries three endpoints in order: OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions → legacy /asr → whisper.cpp /inference (e.g. whisper-server -m ggml-small.bin --port 8000). Default http://127.0.0.1:8000. If unreachable, check: 1) the service is running; 2) CORS is enabled (whisper.cpp has it by default); 3) the firewall allows the port.
cfg.fwModelDesc: Name of the model loaded by the service (common: tiny / base / small / medium / large-v2 / large-v3 — bigger is more accurate but slower). With whisper.cpp (whisper-server), the model is fixed by the -m startup flag; what you type here is display-only.
cfg.geminiTitle: Gemini API Key (only needed for "Gemini Cloud")
cfg.geminiDesc: Only needed for AI summaries with the "Gemini Cloud" service. Save up to 5 keys and switch when one fails. Leave empty when using Local Ollama.
cfg.geminiGuide: No Gemini API Key yet? Tap here for the setup guide
cfg.geminiStep1: Open aistudio.google.com/app/apikey (Google AI Studio API key page)
cfg.geminiStep2: Log in with your Google account (same as Gmail/Drive); first visit may ask you to accept terms
cfg.geminiStep4: If asked for a Google Cloud project, pick "Create API key in new project" — simplest, no extra setup
cfg.geminiStep5: Copy the key starting with AIza (you can revisit this page later, unlike Groq — but copy it now anyway)
cfg.geminiStep6: Come back here and paste it into the input above
cfg.geminiNote: The free tier is enough for daily use, no credit card. Keys stay in this device's browser and are never uploaded. Optional — only needed for AI summaries; other features work without it.
cfg.ollamaSumDesc: Used when the summary service is "Local Ollama". Transcripts only go to the address below (can differ from transcription). Default http://127.0.0.1:11434. If unreachable, check ollama serve is running and cross-origin is allowed (OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*).
cfg.sharedDesc:
Save the current Groq/Gemini key pools and service choices to the server's api.json; other devices on the same URL can "Load from server" to share them without typing. ⚠️ api.json on a server is publicly readable — only suitable for a trusted intranet/home server. Never put truly sensitive keys in it. Local Ollama/Faster-Whisper need no keys; addresses and models are shared too. Empty key pools are skipped on load, keeping local values. When this page loads, an api.json found on the server is automatically applied over local settings (including interface language).
Note: purely static hosts (e.g. GitHub Pages) reject writes, so "Save to server" will fail — use "Download api.json" and place it next to this page manually instead.
cfg.dangerDesc: Wipes all API keys, card drafts, summaries, share-resume records, and read-notice records on this device. Irreversible — useful after using a shared device.
m.dontShow: Don't show again for this version
m.recBody: This tool only does "live speech-to-text". Once audio becomes text, the original recording is discarded — nothing is kept or uploaded for storage. But transcription sends the audio to your selected service (Groq Cloud or your Ollama address). If you want a backup of the raw audio, record one separately with your phone's built-in recorder; the two are independent.
m.clearIntro: This clears what this device and browser have stored:
m.clearLi1: Your Groq/Gemini API keys (Ollama needs no key; only addresses and model preferences are kept)
m.clearLi2: "Don't remind me" records (prompts will show again next time)
m.clearLi3: Voice cards not yet sent (cards auto-save so you can recover from accidental navigation — but clearing deletes them irreversibly)
m.clearMid: ⚠️ What this tool cannot clear: if you used "copy to clipboard", notes may remain in the system clipboard (a phone/browser mechanism web pages cannot wipe). On a shared device, copy some unrelated text afterwards to overwrite it.
m.clearConfirm: Are you sure? You will need to re-enter API keys to keep recording, and current card content cannot be recovered.

m.sumLineDesc: Pick a friend or group from the LINE list to send the summary text. Only works when opened inside LINE; regular browsers fall back to system share or copy.
m.sumOtherDesc: Opens the system share sheet. Unavailable inside LINE — falls back to LINE friend share.

m.noticeBody:
Before you start, please know this

  • Speech recognition offers "Groq Cloud" (free, bring your own API key — see the Settings guide), "Local Ollama", or "Local Faster-Whisper" (the latter two need no key; addresses and models are set separately under "🎙️ Transcription service")
  • API keys live in this device's browser. On a public or shared device (e.g. office computer, borrowed phone), clear them via the "shared device" section below, or manually afterwards, so the next user cannot see your keys and notes
  • Once audio becomes text, the raw recording is not kept — only text cards. To keep a copy, record one separately with a phone recorder app
  • Transcription uploads the audio to your selected service (Groq Cloud, or your Ollama/Faster-Whisper address). If the address is your own computer, audio never leaves it
  • Audio auto-splits every 15 seconds for transcription; a sentence spanning the cut may become two cards. Known limitation
  • Organized voice cards auto-save in this device's browser — accidental navigation or refresh will not lose them. On a shared device, be sure to clear local data via the API key card afterwards
  • Three ways to send: "Send to chat" works only when opened inside a LINE chat; "LINE friend share" likewise only in LINE (both optional); "System share / copy" works in any browser with no login at all; inside LINE, system share falls back to friend share (in-app browser limitation)
  • "Shared notes" is read-only: it only reads content others pasted into the shared Google Sheet (tick multiple entries, mix with your own cards for a combined summary) and never writes back. To add your organized content or a generated summary, use "Copy as Sheet-paste format" / "Save to Sheet" and paste manually
m.consentBody:
This is a personal side-project tool for turning speech into text cards. No LINE login and no official-account friending needed — just open it in a regular browser (Chrome/Safari). Please confirm you understand the following:

  • Speech recognition offers "Groq Cloud" (bring your own API key), "Local Ollama" (keyless, default http://127.0.0.1:11434), or "Local Faster-Whisper" (keyless, default http://127.0.0.1:8000), switchable under "🎙️ Transcription service". Keys stay in this device's browser
  • Your recorded audio is uploaded to the selected transcription service (Groq Cloud, or your Ollama/Faster-Whisper address). Raw audio is never kept — only the transcribed text. If the address is your own computer, audio never leaves it
  • AI summaries default to Google Gemini Cloud (optional, bring your own key); likewise switchable to Local Ollama under "🧠 Meeting summary", in which case transcripts only go to your local address
  • "🔗 Shared API keys" can store keys in the server's api.json for multi-device sharing, but that file is publicly readable — only suitable for a trusted intranet. Never put sensitive keys in it
  • Organized voice card content is likewise stored in this device's browser for recovery after accidental navigation; on a shared device, clear it afterwards too
  • This tool is not recommended for truly confidential or highly sensitive content (trade secrets, others' personal data, passwords, ID numbers, etc.)
  • This is a personally maintained tool with no formal support or service guarantee and may change or be discontinued

Clicking "I have read and agree" means you understand and accept the risks above. If you disagree, please close this page.

g.p1: Open sheets.new for a blank sheet (or reuse an existing one). No header row needed — every cell holds one complete entry, filling down from A1.

g.p2: On the Notes or Summary tab, tap "Copy as Sheet-paste format" (or "Save to Sheet" for summaries). You will be asked for a topic name, then a complete data blob is copied to the clipboard. Back in Google Sheets:
g.li3: The next person clicks A2, then A3, and so on — always paste into the next empty cell
g.pNote: Each cell looks like a long jumble of letters, numbers, and symbols (e.g. {"label":"First half transcript",...}). That is normal — this sheet is a database for the app to read, not a table for humans. Do not reformat it by hand.
g.h3: ③ Set sharing permission and get the link
g.p3: Click "Share" (top right) → "Get link", and set the permission to:
g.permOkSub: This is the only permission this tool needs. Anyone with the link can "read" the content, but nobody (including this tool) can modify or delete the sheet.
g.pLink: Copy the link, paste it into this tool's "Shared" tab input, and tap "Load".
g.sec1: This tool only reads data — it has zero ability to write to Google Sheets. Even with "Editor" permission, it cannot and will not modify your sheet.
g.sec2: But the "link can edit" setting itself is risky regardless of this tool — it is how Google Sheets works: with "Anyone with the link" + "Editor", anyone holding the link (not just your collaborators — anyone it gets forwarded to, indexed by search engines, or shared to the wrong place) can edit, delete, or even wipe the whole sheet, no login required.
g.sec3: This tool only ever needs "Viewer" permission. Always pick "Viewer", never "Editor". Give collaborators who truly need to write their own edit rights via individual email invites instead of opening editing to the whole internet.
